The institution of Reddit was stress tested and it failed.

Free speech is not negotiable. Reddit has made it clear that its institutional policy is to limit speech and only accommodate safe and majority supported ideas. For example, right now the safe spaces concept provides a place that restricts criticism of obesity, feminism, and LGBT communities.

In the future, if Reddit's leaders or business managers were to decide those communities are taboo (the way those communities have been treated throughout most of human history in fact), then only criticism of the obese, feminists, and LGBT could become permissible. Three hundred years ago what would today be considered feminists were given broad public support and great autonomy in otherwise feudal Europe. Then one day the public perception shifted and those same individuals were suddenly being burned at the stakes as witches. History is nothing if not cyclical.

It is reasonable to assume that future leaders of Reddit could decide that all defense of LGBT individuals is unsafe and begin shadowbanning defenders of that community- if for no other reason than it suddenly becomes bad for business to support minority groups.

No minority group has ever been protected or advanced in the long run by limiting criticism and speech about that group. History has shown that they are very often harmed as soon as the pendulum inevitably swings back the other way. That is why speech cannot be limited. It only ever ends up hurting the very people the censorship was originally intended to protect.

Ms. Pao is merely the unfortunate figure head at the top who codified the vile censorship policy for the institution. Reddit's staff have determined that censorship is the standard they work under. The next leader would merely be a new unfortunate figure head.

The institution of Reddit was tested and it failed spectacularly. So, no I would not go back if the failed institution were to change its figure head.

I find it weird how a ton of people keep bringing up the whole "Free speech protection is meant to protect you from GOVERNMENTS, not CORPORATIONS!" angle when minimizing Reddit's actions this week without considering the discrepancy between what Reddit says they stand for and what they are actually doing. Yes, I do agree that Reddit is a company and thus they have full control over their platform and what they allow users to post on it, but the problem is that Reddit has always (and still does) advertised itself as a free speech platform, which sets the expectation that all law abiding content, even if you personally disagree with it, can be hosted on the site. Then comes Pao and the gradual push to promote safety and inclusiveness which culminated this week to the sanctioning of subreddit bans. Anyway you cut it the content that was banned broke no laws or established Reddit rules (even while SRS flagrantly does) which demonstrated the move to ban content was based entirely on specific ideologies, contrary to free speech. It would have been better if they just fully embraced this new direction and removed any self promotion as a free speech platform as they would have at least been honest with themselves and with their users, but of course if they did that then it would probably have caused a bigger shit storm and Voat would still be offline trying to cope with all the new users.

In order for Reddit to get back in good standing with me they would have to pull a complete 180 to show their commitment to being a free speech platform. Pao would need to be fired, banned subreddits re-instated, a public apology given from admins to take ownership of their actions, and other major changes would need to happen to the site like greater transparency and the ceasing of shadowbans. Even then I think the relationship between Reddit and some of its users is irreparable, and if Reddit actually did any of the things I mentioned I'll happily eat my shorts.

That being the case, here I am on Voat, and I expect I'll be staying here while I watch Redd-tanic sink.
